info.title: Attome XRM API
info.description: The Attome XRM platform's HTTP API. Entity record shapes under `/api/v1/{entity}` are resolved from each deployment's runtime metadata (D-003) and therefore cannot be enumerated statically — those operations document the generic envelope only. Fetch `GET /api/v1/schema/{logicalname}` for a live entity's fields.

get.description:
Every web portal with its keyword, type, whether it is on, its owning team and MFA policy,
one-based pages. User administrators only.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
One-based (D-347): page 1 is the first page. Values below 1 are
clamped up to 1 rather than rejected, matching the legacy lists.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description:
Rows per page, clamped to `1..=MAX_PAGE_SIZE`. Defaults to
`DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`.

post.description:
A portal with its URL keyword, type, owning team (the staff team that owns what its users create)
and MFA policy. User administrators only. Audited.

422.description: Request failed validation

get.description: One portal's settings and `row_version`. User administrators only.

The account policy of one web portal: who may sign up, with which role,
and how its accounts sign in (D-588). Administrators only.

put.description:
Replaces the account policy of one web portal: who may sign up, with
which role, and how its accounts sign in (D-588). Administrators only.
Audited.

422.description: Request failed validation

get.description: G12-T3: the domain the portal is served on, if any. User administrators only.

put.summary: Serve a web portal on its own domain
put.description:
G12-T3: sets the domain the portal is served on (`null` clears it). Point the domain's DNS at
this server; with ACME on, its certificate is ordered at the next restart. User administrators
only. Audited.

422.description: Not a host name

get.description:
Per entity, the lookup field to the portal user that a portal create fills in. Role
administrators only.

put.description:
Sets, or clears with `null`, the lookup field on the entity that a portal create fills with the
portal user. Role administrators only. Audited.

422.description: Not a lookup to webportal_user, or made writable by a grant

get.description:
The erasure requests of the portal's users, with their status, one-based pages. Compliance
administrators only.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
One-based (D-347): page 1 is the first page. Values below 1 are
clamped up to 1 rather than rejected, matching the legacy lists.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description:
Rows per page, clamped to `1..=MAX_PAGE_SIZE`. Defaults to
`DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`.

post.description:
Closes an open erasure request without erasing, for example under a legal hold; the account is
untouched. Compliance administrators only. Audited.

404.description: No open request with this id in this portal

get.description: The portal's roles with how many users hold each. Role administrators only.

200.description: Every role of the portal, by name (one page)

post.description: A named role of the portal, with no grants yet. Role administrators only. Audited.

409.description: Name already used in this portal

422.description: Request failed validation

get.description: One role with how many users hold it and its entity grants. Role administrators only.

200.description: The role with every grant, condition and field row

404.description: No such role in this portal

delete.description: Removes the role and its grants. Role administrators only. Audited.

404.description: No such role in this portal

409.description: Users still hold it, or the signup policy hands it out

404.description: No such role in this portal

409.description: Name already used in this portal

422.description: Invalid name

put.summary: Grant a portal role access to an entity
put.description:
Sets what the role may do on the entity (read, create, update, delete), on which records (one to
three conditions, ANDed, such as `account_ref` equal to `@portal_user.account_ref`) and on which
fields (read, write, filter). Replaces any grant it had there. Role administrators only. Audited.

404.description: No such role in this portal

422.description: Invalid grant: no condition, a denied entity or field, and so on

delete.summary: Remove a portal role's grant on an entity
delete.description: The role's users may do nothing more on that entity. Role administrators only. Audited.

patch.description:
Changes the keyword, type, on or off, owning team (`null` clears it) or MFA policy given, when
`row_version` is the stored one. User administrators only. Audited.

409.description: Stale row_version, or keyword already in use

422.description: Request failed validation

get.description:
The portal's users with their name, email or username and status, one-based pages. User
administrators only.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
One-based (D-347): page 1 is the first page. Values below 1 are
clamped up to 1 rather than rejected, matching the legacy lists.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description:
Rows per page, clamped to `1..=MAX_PAGE_SIZE`. Defaults to
`DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`.

post.description:
A portal user with a name and an email or username (at least one), in `invited` status with no
password; the password is set when the invitation is accepted. User administrators only. Audited.

409.description: Email already used in this portal

422.description: Request failed validation

delete.description:
Deletes the user's credentials, ending every session, and marks the profile deleted and disabled;
a restored profile has no credential and cannot sign in. User administrators only. Audited.

404.description: No such user in this portal

post.description:
The user cannot sign in, and every session they hold ends at once. User administrators only.
Audited.

404.description: No such user in this portal

post.description:
Returns the user to `active` when a password is set, otherwise to `invited`. User administrators
only. Audited.

404.description: No such user in this portal

post.description:
Scrubs the user's personal fields in place, keeping the id so their records and audit rows still
resolve (to "Erased user"), and removes every credential, session, token, role and pending
signup; consent records stay as evidence. The open erasure request is completed, or one is
recorded. Compliance administrators only. Audited.

200.description: Personal data scrubbed in place; credentials, sessions and links removed

404.description: No such user in this portal

post.description:
Records a data subject access request for the user and fulfils it, so the export stays in the
request list as evidence. Compliance administrators only. Audited.

200.description: A data-subject access request was recorded under the user's email and fulfilled: masked NDJSON files for the profile (every portal account with that email), the consent history and any memory rows, each checksum-verified

404.description: No such user in this portal

post.description:
Emails the user an invitation link to set a password, the token and the email queued in one
transaction; refused when email is switched off. User administrators only. Audited.

202.description: Invitation emailed; older unused links are void

404.description: No such user in this portal

409.description: The user has already accepted an invitation

503.description: Email is not configured on this deployment

put.summary: Give a portal user a role
put.description: Sets the user's role in the portal. Role administrators only. Audited.

204.description: The user's one role is set

404.description: No such user or role in this portal

delete.summary: Take a portal user's role away
delete.description:
The user keeps their account but holds no role, and so none of its grants. Role administrators
only. Audited.

204.description: The user holds no role now and reaches no records

404.description: The user holds no role in this portal

post.description:
F9-T6: a person with update access approves or rejects. Approval marks the matched account a
partner, or creates one, and invites its administrator to the portal, in one transaction. Audited.

403.description: Not a person, or no update access

404.description: No such application the caller may read

409.description: Already decided, or the email has a portal account

422.description: No reason to reject, or no portal to approve into

get.summary: The web portal on this host
get.description:
G12-T3: the keyword of the enabled web portal served on the request's host, so the web app
opens it at `/`. No sign-in; 404 when no portal uses the host.

What changed about the portal's accounts since a time (a password change, reset, disable or sign-out
everywhere moves the credential epoch; erasure removes the account), so a trusted server can end
its own sessions within one pull.

403.description: Not a privileged S2S client, or trusted login is off

get.summary: Read a portal account for a trusted server
get.description: The account's email (masked) and MFA state, for the user's own account screen.

403.description: Not a privileged S2S client, or trusted login is off

post.summary: Add an email to a portal account
post.description:
After the password again, sends a link to the new address; it is added only when its owner opens
it. When another account of the portal has the address, its owner is told instead, with the same
answer.

403.description: Not a privileged S2S client, or trusted login is off

422.description: Malformed body

post.summary: Confirm MFA for a portal account
post.description: A code from the authenticator app turns MFA on; the recovery codes come back once.

403.description: Not a privileged S2S client, or trusted login is off

post.summary: Turn MFA off for a portal account
post.description: After the password and a current code; refused while the portal requires MFA.

403.description: Not a privileged S2S client, or trusted login is off

post.summary: Start MFA for a portal account
post.description:
After the password again, a new secret for the user's authenticator app, in force once a code from
it confirms it.

403.description: Not a privileged S2S client, or trusted login is off

post.summary: Check a portal login for a trusted server
post.description:
For a portal's own trusted server, over S2S: checks a portal user's credentials and answers with
the decision; a refusal is an outcome, not an error.

200.description: The decision (see `outcome`); refusals are outcomes, not errors

403.description: The client lacks webportal.trusted_login, or the portal doesn't allow trusted login

422.description: Malformed body (e.g. client_ip is not an address)

post.description:
The emailed link that adds an address to a portal account: the address is written, verified, only
now, and the address it replaces, if any, is told.

204.description: The email is on the account

409.description: Another account has used this address since the link was sent

422.description: The link is invalid, used or expired

post.description:
Sets the invited user's password from the invitation token; the account becomes active and its
email verified. An invalid or expired invitation, or a password that fails the policy, is 422.

204.description: Password set; the account is active and its email verified

422.description: Invalid or expired invitation, or the password fails policy

post.summary: Sign in to a web portal

200.description: Logged in; portal session cookies set

post.summary: Sign out of a web portal
post.description: Ends the session and clears the portal's cookies.

Turns MFA on with a code from the pending secret and returns new recovery codes, shown once. A
wrong code, or no pending enrolment, is 422.

200.description: MFA enabled; the new recovery codes, shown once

422.description: Wrong code or no pending enrollment

post.description:
Turns the portal user's MFA off for an authenticator code; refused (422) on a portal that requires
MFA.

422.description: Wrong code, or the portal requires MFA

post.description:
A pending TOTP secret for the signed-in portal user to add to an authenticator app; it takes
effect only once confirmed with a code.

200.description: A pending TOTP secret; confirm it with a code

post.description: A new set of recovery codes, shown once, for an authenticator code; the old set stops working.

200.description: A new set of recovery codes, shown once; the old set is void

422.description: Wrong authenticator code, or MFA is not enabled

post.summary: Link an identity provider to a portal account
post.description:
Finishes a pending link with proof of the existing account and signs in; an unknown, used or
expired link, or a failed proof, is 401.

401.description: The pending link is unknown, used or expired, or the account proof failed

post.summary: Finish an identity provider sign-in with MFA
post.description:
Sends the MFA code for a provider sign-in that needs one and signs in; an unknown, used or expired
step, or a wrong code, is 401.

401.description: The pending step is unknown, used or expired, or the code is wrong

get.summary: Finish signing in with an identity provider
get.description:
Where the provider sends the browser back. Redirects (303) to the portal app: home when signed in,
a page that finishes a pending link or MFA step, or the login page with one error, whatever went
wrong.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The authorization code the provider sent back.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The state value this sign-in started with.

200.description: Not returned: every accepted request gets a 303 redirect. Listed because every documented operation declares a 2xx.

303.description: Redirect to the portal app: signed in, a pending link or MFA step, or the login page with an error

get.summary: Start signing in with an identity provider
get.description:
Redirects (303) to one of the portal's OIDC providers, after binding the flow to this portal,
provider and browser so a sign-in cannot be planted in someone else's browser.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: An OIDC provider key the portal offers

200.description: Not returned: every accepted request gets a 303 redirect. Listed because every documented operation declares a 2xx.

404.description: No such portal, or the portal doesn't offer this provider

post.description:
Rotates the refresh token and sets new session cookies; a missing, expired or reused refresh token
is 401, and a reused one ends its whole family.

200.description: Rotated; new portal session cookies set

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired or reused refresh token

post.description:
Sets a new password from a reset link's token and ends every existing session; an invalid or
expired link, or a password that fails the policy, is 422. Rate limited.

204.description: Password reset; every existing session ended

422.description: Invalid or expired link, or the password fails policy

post.summary: Ask for a portal password reset
post.description:
Emails a reset link when the address has an account; the answer is the same either way, so it
tells nobody whether an account exists. Rate limited. 503 when email is not configured.

200.description: Always the same answer, whether or not the address has an account

503.description: Email is not configured on this deployment

post.summary: Sign up to a web portal
post.description:
Asks for an account with an email, a password and the portal's current consent versions. The
answer is 202 whatever happened (a verification link, a notice to an existing account, or nothing),
so it reveals no account. A password that fails the policy, a consent that does not match, or a
failed CAPTCHA is 422.

202.description: Accepted. The same answer whatever happened: a verification link, a notice to an existing account, or nothing

422.description: The password fails policy, the consent doesn't match the portal's current versions, or the CAPTCHA failed

post.description:
Creates the account from the emailed verification link; sign in with the password given at signup.
An invalid, used or expired link, or a portal whose signup closed, is 422.

204.description: Account created; sign in with the password given at signup

422.description: The link is invalid, used or expired, or signup is no longer open

get.description:
The portal user's own profile and `row_version`. On a portal that requires MFA, a user not yet
enrolled reaches only the MFA and sign-out routes.

403.description: MFA enrollment required first, or cross-site request

patch.summary: Change the signed-in portal user's profile
patch.description:
Changes the profile fields the portal lets users edit (never email, status, lookups or files).
Requires `If-Match` with the profile's `row_version`; a stale one is 409. Needs the portal's
current consent.

200.description: Updated; the profile as GET /me returns it

403.description: A field this portal doesn't let users edit (email, status, lookups and files never are), or consent is missing

422.description: Invalid value, or If-Match missing

get.description: The portal's current consent versions and whether the signed-in user accepted them.

200.description: The portal's current versions, and whether they're accepted

post.description: Records the user's acceptance of the portal's current versions; other versions are 422.

422.description: Not the portal's current versions

post.summary: Ask for my portal account to be erased
post.description:
Sends the request to staff, who erase or reject it; an open request is returned rather than a
second one made.

202.description: Staff have the request; an open one is returned rather than duplicated

post.description:
Changes the password given the current one; every other session ends and this one is issued
again. A wrong current password, or a new one that fails the policy, is 422.

204.description: Changed; every other session ended, this one re-issued

422.description: Wrong current password, or the new one fails policy

get.description:
R1-T2: the privacy requests the signed-in person made, newest first, with their status and
deadline.

post.description:
R1-T2: a privacy (data subject) request about the signed-in person: a copy of their data,
erasure, portability, objection, restriction of processing or rectification. They give their
password again to prove who they are; the subject is their verified email address. Staff work
it with every other data subject request, by the deadline the deployment's law sets.

422.description: The password is wrong, or an unknown request type

get.description: The signed-in user's live sessions, to end the ones they do not recognise.

post.description: Ends every session of the user except this one.

delete.summary: End one of my portal sessions

404.description: No such portal, or no such live session of yours

get.summary: List the entities a portal user can use
get.description: The entities the caller's role has a grant on (at most 100). Needs the portal's current consent.

200.description: The entities the caller's role has a grant on (page 1, at most 100; `total` counts them all)

403.description: Consent to the portal's current terms is missing

get.summary: Describe an entity for a portal user
get.description:
What the caller's role may do on the entity and the fields it may read or write. Needs the
portal's current consent.

200.description: The entity's actions and the fields the caller may read or write

403.description: Consent to the portal's current terms is missing

404.description: No such portal, or no access to this entity (indistinguishable from a missing one)

get.description:
The published pages for portal users (audience `portal` or `public`), at most 100, the
deployment's own first, for the portal app's navigation. Needs a portal session and the
portal's current consent.

403.description: Consent to the portal's current terms is missing

get.description:
A published page for portal users, by name, with a record page's entity by logical name. Needs a
portal session and the portal's current consent. A page for staff only is 404.

403.description: Consent to the portal's current terms is missing

404.description: No such portal, or no such portal page

post.description:
F9-T6: anyone may apply, through the same limits and CAPTCHA as sign-up. The answer says nothing
about whether the company is known. Audited.

422.description: A field is invalid, or the CAPTCHA failed

post.description: F9-T4: only the partner the lead is offered to, before the limit. Audited.

404.description: No such portal, or no live offer to the caller's partner

post.description:
F9-T4: only the partner the lead is offered to, before the limit; the lead stops naming the
partner. Audited.

404.description: No such portal, or no live offer to the caller's partner

get.description: F10-T12: the statement of the signed-in person's own partner account, for one period.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based: page 1 is the first page.

401.description: Not signed in to the portal

404.description: No such portal, or nothing for the caller's partner in the period

get.description:
The records of the entity inside the caller's role scope, one-based pages up to the portal's cap,
sorted by a filterable field; any other query key is an equality filter on a filterable field.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based: page 1 is the first page.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: At most the portal's page-size cap (100 or less)

200.description: Records in the caller's scope; any other query key is an equality filter on a filterable field

404.description: No such portal, or no access to this entity

422.description: Unknown or non-filterable field

post.summary: Create a record in a portal
post.description:
Creates a record through the shared entity engine, owned by the portal's team and naming the portal
user, when the role may create it and write every field given; a record that would fall outside
the caller's scope is 422. An idempotency key replays the first result.

parameters.name: x-idempotency-key
parameters.description: Replays the first result for a repeated key instead of creating twice

201.description: Created; owned by the portal's team, recording the portal user

403.description: Not allowed to create, or a field is not writable

404.description: No such portal, or no access to this entity

422.description: Invalid, or the record would be outside the caller's scope

get.summary: Get a record in a portal
get.description: One record inside the caller's scope, with the fields the role may read.

404.description: Not found or not in scope (indistinguishable)

delete.summary: Delete a record in a portal
delete.description:
Deletes a record inside the caller's scope when the role may, with its `If-Match` row version; a
record with dependents is 409.

404.description: Not found or not in scope (indistinguishable)

409.description: Stale row_version, or the entity has dependents

patch.summary: Change a record in a portal
patch.description:
Changes fields the role may write, with the record's `If-Match` row version; a change that would
move the record out of the caller's scope is 422.

404.description: Not found or not in scope (indistinguishable)

422.description: Invalid, or the change would move the record out of scope

get.summary: Download a record's file in a portal
get.description:
A short-lived URL serving the file as an attachment, when the role can read the field; a
multi-file field needs `key`.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: A file field the caller's role can read

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Which file, for a multi-file field (one of the keys the record shows).

200.description: A short-lived download URL (the file is served as an attachment)

404.description: No such record, not in scope, a field the caller can't read, or no file (indistinguishable)

422.description: A multi-file field without ?key=, or a stored key outside this record's own prefix (only on an in-scope record)

post.summary: Start a file upload in a portal
post.description:
An upload session and a short-lived URL to PUT the bytes to, in quarantine, for a file field the
role can write; content type, size, storage quota and the number of open sessions are limited.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: A file field the caller's role can write

200.description: A session and a presigned PUT to its quarantine key

404.description: No such record, not in scope, or a field the caller can't write (indistinguishable)

409.description: An upload for this field is already being created

422.description: Content type or size not allowed, or a storage quota would be exceeded

429.description: Too many upload sessions for this account or portal

x-audit-exempt.note: only records upload intent; the scan result (FileScanned) and the record write naming the file (Entity/Update) are audited on their own paths

get.description: The session's progress; once `clean`, `final_key` is the value to write on the record's field.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: A file field the caller's role can write

200.description: The session's progress; once `clean`, `final_key` is the value to write on the record's field

404.description: No such record, writable file field, or session of yours (indistinguishable)

post.description: Marks the upload `uploaded` and queues its scan, or `rejected`; a finalised session is 409.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: A file field the caller's role can write

404.description: No such record, writable file field, or session of yours (indistinguishable)

x-audit-exempt.note: moves the session to uploaded and enqueues the scan; the scan result (FileScanned) and the record write naming the file (Entity/Update) are audited on their own paths

outcome.description:
`sent` (email: a link went to the address, or, when another account
has it, a notice did: the answer is the same), `unchanged`,
`invalid_email`, `ok` (MFA), `already_enabled`, `wrong_code`,
`required` (the portal requires MFA: it can't be turned off),
`bad_credentials` (the password), `rate_limited` or `unavailable`
(the account is disabled or gone, or email isn't set up).

recovery_codes.description: MFA confirm: the recovery codes, shown once.

secret.description:
MFA enroll: the new secret (base32) and its `otpauth://` URI, for
the player's authenticator app. Not in force until confirmed.

auth_epoch.description: Sessions issued under an older epoch are revoked.

next_since.description: Pass as `since` next time (the newest `changed_at`, or `since`).

allowed_cidrs.description:
Client addresses allowed to reach the portal, as CIDRs or single
addresses. Empty means any address. Outside it, every portal route
answers the same 404 as an unknown portal (G-13).

editable_profile_fields.description: `webportal_user` fields a user may edit on their own profile.

page_size_cap.description: The largest page a portal list returns, 1 to 100 (R10, G-13).

records_rpm.description: Portal-wide ceiling on record-route requests per minute (G-4).

row_version.description: Echo it back on the next write (optimistic concurrency).

signup_role_ref.description: The portal role a self-registered or OIDC-created user gets.

trusted_server_login.description:
D-779: the portal's own servers (S2S clients granted
`webportal.trusted_login`) may sign users in with a password and
create accounts for free usernames. Off by default.

username_blocked_words.description: D-777: words no username may contain (case-insensitive).

username_min_len.description: D-777: username length, in characters (defaults 3 and 12).

username_reserved.description:
D-777: whole usernames nobody may take (case-insensitive), e.g.
"admin", "support", staff names.

value.description: A literal (an array for `in`). Exactly one of `value` and `value_ref`.

value_ref.description:
`@portal_user.id`, or `@portal_user.<lookup field>` (e.g.
`@portal_user.account_ref`). Only with `eq`. Resolved per request; a
null or missing value matches no row.

`field` may be `id`, the record's own key, with `eq` only: that is how
a role reaches the portal user's own parent record
(`id = @portal_user.company_ref`).

accepted.description:
The signed-in user has accepted the current versions (always true when
the portal requires none).

portal_user_field.description:
A lookup on the entity to `webportal_user`, set to the portal user
on every portal create. `null` to clear.

ErrorDetails.description:
`ErrorResponse.details`: its shape depends on the `error` code —
a list of [`FieldError`] on `validation_error`, [`RuleViolationDetails`] on
`rule_violation`, [`FieldLockedDetails`] on `field_locked` and
`field_locked_required` (D-789).

ErrorResponse.description: Standard error envelope. `error` is a stable machine-readable code; `message` is human-readable and never contains internal detail.

current_state.description:
Present on a version conflict: the server's current row for the
fields the caller touched, as a JSON object. The owning engine filters
sensitive columns out before building it (BTY-16c's precondition), so
this is a deliberate filtered projection — never a raw row dump.

current_version.description:
Present on a version conflict: the `row_version` the server currently
holds, so a caller can re-read and retry instead of guessing what the
winner wrote. Omitted when the conflict is not version-based.

oneOf.description:
Structured detail, shaped by `error` (see [`ErrorDetails`]): every
field-level failure on a `validation_error` response when the raiser
has a field list, so a form can render them all at once; every firing
rule on a `rule_violation` response from a business rule; every
refused field on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`. Omitted
otherwise.

error.description:
Stable machine-readable code — `not_found`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`,
`attribute_not_writable`, `limit_exceeded`,
`conflict`, `version_conflict`, `duplicate_detected`, `idempotency_conflict`,
`validation_error`, `customer_tests_failed`, `feature_unavailable`, `feature_hidden`,
`rate_limit_exceeded`, `overloaded`, `capability_unavailable`,
`metadata_authoring_locked`, `transition_not_allowed`,
`rule_violation`, `field_locked`, `field_locked_required`,
`reauth_required`, `server_timeout`, `query_timeout`, `read_only`, `payload_too_large`,
`request_rejected`, `invalid_cursor`, `resync_needed`, `cascade_restricted`,
`idempotency_outcome_unknown`, `idempotency_replay_unavailable`,
`method_not_allowed`, or
`internal_error` — one per `AppError` variant (`FieldLocked` answers
two: plain and required) (`attome-types/src/error.rs`); M01 Core C-23
found this list four codes short of the taxonomy it documents.

errors.description:
Every field-level failure on a `validation_error`, as
`{attribute, rule, message, fix}`.

field.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the first
refused field (every one is in `details.fields`); on
`attribute_not_writable` (Q15-T4): the attribute the caller may not
write.

hidden.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected`: how many more matches the caller may
not read.

instance.description: The request path the problem happened at.

matches.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected` (A15-T4): the existing records the
save matches that the caller may read (record, rule, score).

request_id.description:
Present on responses that passed through the request-id middleware
(D-043); absent on the few pre-middleware rejection paths.

retry_after_sec.description:
Present on a `rate_limit_exceeded` response when the limiter knows its
window: seconds to wait before retrying, equal by construction to the
`Retry-After` header on the same response (BTY-11a). Omitted when the
limit that was hit has no known window.

retryable.description:
Whether the same request may succeed later (the error catalogue's
verdict for `code`).

rule_id.description:
Present on a `rule_violation` response (D-472): the id of the
`xrm_core_rule` whose failing expression produced this 422, so a
client can highlight or re-check the exact rule without parsing
`message`. Omitted on every other code, and on any response that
does not name a rule.
Also present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the
business rule that locks `field`.

rule_name.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`: the display name
of the rule that locks `field`.

title.description:
A short title for `code` in the request's language (Z14-T3), e.g.
`The resource was not found.`

type.description: Z14-T1 (RFC 9457): `about:blank`; the problem is named by `code`.

FieldError.description:
One field-level failure inside `ErrorResponse.details` (BTY-16b): the
field the caller sent, a stable machine-readable `code` the client maps
to localized text (e.g. `required`, `too_long`, `invalid_format`,
`not_allowed`), and the English server-side `message`.

A list, not a single error, so one 422 can answer with every bad field at
once (BTY-F11) instead of making a form discover them one round-trip at a
time.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable failure code for this field, independent of
the message text.

field.description:
The offending field, as the caller addressed it (e.g. `email` or
`amount`).

message.description: Human-readable, English, server-side detail for this field.

FieldLockedDetails.description:
`details` of a `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` response: every
refused field, the first being the one the top-level `field` names.

allow_sensitive.description: Required to list an `is_sensitive` field at all.

id.description: The DSR request this export fulfilled.

GrantView.description:
A grant as stored, with the G-3 label: `public` when no condition is bound
to the portal user, which only a read-only grant may be.

expires_at.description: When the emailed link stops working. The link itself is never returned.

LockedField.description:
One field a business rule locks for the writer (D-789 §3.5): `effect` is
`hidden` or `disabled`. No value is ever echoed.

code.description: The current TOTP code, when the account has MFA enrolled.

email.description:
The email; kept for clients from before `login` (D-777). Ignored when
`login` is set.

login.description: D-777: the username or the email (an email contains `@`).

is_enabled.description: Defaults to false: a new portal serves nothing until it is enabled.

owning_team_ref.description: The staff team that owns records portal users create (D-576 item 7).

NewPortalUser.description: D-777: at least one of `email` and `username`.

code.description: The account's TOTP or recovery code, when it has MFA enabled.

PaginatedResponse_CommissionStatementRow.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

amount.description: Absent when the caller may not see pay amounts.

explanation.description: A line's explanation steps; an adjustment's reason.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

items.description:
One entity the caller's role has a grant on. Its actions and fields:
`GET /{keyword}/api/v1/metadata/{entity}`.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;

items.description: One page a portal may show, for its navigation.

items.description:
A record as a portal sees it: only allowlisted fields, no owner,
organisation or staff attribution columns.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;

email.description: D-777: optional when the user has a username.

username.description:
D-777: the login username (case kept); optional when the user has an
email.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PartnerApplicationBody.description: A public partner application, with the CAPTCHA token sign-up takes.

portal_id.description: The portal the partner's administrator signs in to; required to approve.

PartnerLead.description: The lead after an offer or an answer.

PortalDomain.description: A portal's own domain; `null` when it has none.

domain.description: The host name, e.g. `support.example.com`; `null` clears it.

PortalDsrRequest.description:
R1-T2: a request as the person who made it through a web portal sees
it, for tracking: never the subject reference or staff notes.

due_at.description: When it must be answered by, under the deployment's law.

PortalEntityView.description: One entity as a portal may see it in metadata.

PortalFieldView.description: One field as a portal may see it in metadata (web-portal plan Phase 5).

label.description: The field's display label, when it has one.

lookup_entity.description:
For a lookup the caller may pick a value for: the target entity. Set
only when the caller's role reads that entity, so a form can offer its
records; `None` for every other field, including the portal user field
the engine stamps.

options.description:
A choice field's options; `None` for every other type (a formula's
expression or a masked text's settings never reach a portal).

PortalHost.description: The portal served on the request's host.

email.description: D-777: optional when the account has a username.

profile.description:
The fields this portal lets its users edit, with their values (empty
when none are editable).

row_version.description: The profile's version: send it as `If-Match` on `PATCH /me`.

username.description: D-777: the login username, when the account has one.

PortalPage.description: One page as the portal app renders it.

doc.description: The page document (the page kind's shape), with its `id` and `name`.

entity_name.description: A record page's entity, by logical name.

PortalRecord.description:
A record as a portal sees it: only allowlisted fields, no owner,
organisation or staff attribution columns.

mfa_enrollment_required.description:
The portal requires MFA and this user has no usable authenticator
(never enrolled, or signed in with a recovery code since): only the
MFA enrollment and logout routes are available until they enrol.

recovery_code_used.description: This sign-in spent a recovery code (D-588 item 1).

current.description: The session this request was made with.

PortalSettingsPatch.description:
Every field optional except `row_version`. `owning_team_ref` distinguishes
"absent" (unchanged) from `null` (cleared).

email.description: D-777: optional when the user has a username.

username.description:
D-777: the login username (case kept); optional when the user has an
email.

password.description:
The current password, again: proof that the person asking is the
account's owner.

RecoveryCodes.description: Single-use MFA recovery codes, shown once (D-588 item 1).

RuleFailure.description:
One business-rule `error` policy that fired (D-789 §3.3), inside a
`rule_violation` body's `details.rules`. Carries names and the rule's own
message, never a record value.

field.description: The field the policy is attached to, when it names one.

rule_name.description: The rule's display name (its name when it has none).

RuleViolationDetails.description:
`details` of a `rule_violation` response (D-789): the field of the first
failing policy, when it names one, and every blocking `error` policy that
fired, the first (by rule display order) being the one `rule_id` names.

final_key.description:
Set only once `status = "clean"` — the value the client must PATCH
onto the record's file field. Without this, a polling client would
have no way to learn what the async scan job promoted the object to.

captcha_token.description: The CAPTCHA widget's token, when the deployment configures one.

email.description:
Masked (`z***@example.com`): the owner recognises it; the caller
never needs the address itself.

pending_email.description: Masked: the address a link sent but not yet opened would add.

client_ip.description:
The player's address as the calling server saw it on its own
connection. Used for rate limits and the audit trail.

code.description:
D-780: for an account with MFA, the player's TOTP code or one of their
recovery codes (without it such an account answers `mfa_required`).

create_if_missing.description: Create the account when `login` is a free, valid username.

auth_epoch.description:
The credential epoch: sessions the caller issued under an older
epoch are revoked (password change, disable, log out everywhere).

outcome.description:
`ok`, `created`, `bad_credentials`, `name_rejected`,
`password_rejected`, `disabled`, `rate_limited`, `mfa_required` or
`mfa_failed` (D-780: the code was wrong, replayed or used up).

reason.description: For `name_rejected` and `password_rejected`: why, for the player.

recovery_code_used.description:
D-780: `ok` with a recovery code (one fewer left; the owner is told by
email when the account has one).

retry_after_secs.description: For `rate_limited`: seconds until trying again helps.

username.description: The account's username (case as stored), for `ok` and `created`.

Warning.description:
Something the server did that the caller should know about though the
request succeeded (a value truncated, a default applied, a page clamped):
a stable `code` and English `message`. Sent only when there is one.

portal_session.name: __Secure-wp_{portal}_session
portal_session.description: A web portal user's session cookie, issued by the portal's sign-in; `{portal}` is the portal's keyword (`wp_{portal}_session` on plain-http local dev). Valid only on that portal's own routes.

s2s_hmac.name: x-s2s-signature
s2s_hmac.description: A system-to-system call, signed. Send `x-s2s-client-id`, `x-s2s-key-id`, `x-s2s-timestamp` (Unix milliseconds, within 300 seconds of the server's clock), `x-s2s-nonce` (single use: a repeat is refused) and `x-s2s-signature`: the hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed by the hex-decoded client secret, of `METHOD`, `PATH_AND_QUERY`, the hex SHA-256 of the body, `TIMESTAMP` and `NONCE`, joined by newlines in that order.

session_cookie.name: __Host-session_token
session_cookie.description: Browser session cookie issued by POST /api/v1/auth/login. Mutating requests additionally require the CSRF conditions enforced by `middleware::csrf`.
